Date: 2026-05-04
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Marisa Chen (Redwood AE), Derrick Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (FastLane CTO), Owen Blake (FastLane Head of Platform), Samira Khan (FastLane ML)

Links shared: deck: /redwood/decks/fastlane-onramp.pdf, benchmark sheet: /redwood/benchmarks/fastlane-latency.csv
summary: FastLane is evaluating time-to-first-token and tradeoffs between Redwood hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Primary concerns: data residency, KMS/encryption, latency targets (p99 < 300ms for short prompts), and predictable cost for peak traffic. Redwood AE/SE explained PLG quickstart, free credits, and pilot path (hosted pilot -> dedicated reserved if predictable throughput). Action items: pricing + pilot contract, SE benchmark using FastLane prompts, customer to confirm security stakeholders.
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs
latency vs cost and batching/quantization options
transcript:
[00:00] Marisa (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:07] Priya (FastLane): Priya here, CTO.
[00:09] Owen (FastLane): Owen, Head of Platform.
[00:11] Samira (FastLane): Samira, ML eng.
[00:13] Derrick (Redwood SE): Derrick here, I'll handle the bench and tech details.
[00:18] Marisa: Awesome. Goal for today — understand your constraints and get you to first token quickly. Priya, high level why now?
[00:25] Priya: We're launching a document summarization feature in Q3, need embeddings and generation for search highlights. Main ask is latency for short prompts, cost predictability, and we have compliance about customer data not leaving certain regions.
[00:38] Owen: Also want to know how fast we can go from sign-up to production. We like PLG but for revenue customers we'll probably need dedicated.
[00:45] Marisa: Totally. Redwood supports a PLG self-serve API with free credits to experiment. Typical path is self-serve hosted API to validate models and prompts, then pilot with Dedicated reserved capacity if you need SLO-backed throughput or move to Private for VPC/on-prem.
[01:05] Samira: When you say "time-to-first-token" what does that mean for us? We care about p50/p95/p99.
[01:12] Derrick: Good question. Time-to-first-token depends on a few things: model size, seq length, and warm cache. For hosted we optimize for cold start with continuous warm pools for popular models; average TTF token for a 2k context gen is typically 80-150ms on our tuned variants, but for tiny prompts we're seeing p99s under 250-300ms in many cases. You'll see variance with model choice.
[01:35] Priya: That p99 under 300ms — is that for hosted? If we go private on-prem it'll change right?
[01:41] Derrick: Yes hosted profiles are tuned. Private/on-prem performance depends on your infra. For Dedicated it's our reserved GPU pools — predictable throughput and lower variance because you own capacity. Private gives you control for residency and KMS but you'll need to size for your peak QPS.
[01:57] Owen: On KMS — do you integrate with customer KMS or forced Redwood-managed keys? We have HSM requirements for some customers.
[02:04] Marisa: We support customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS, GCP CMEK) for Private deployments and for Dedicated we can do tenant-level envelope encryption; for hosted we offer Redwood-managed keys but can discuss enterprise key wrapping or HSM integrations for higher tiers.
[02:22] Priya: Ok good. SOC 2 — we need audit logs, SSO, RBAC, and retention controls.
[02:27] Marisa: Redwood has SOC 2, SAML SSO, RBAC, audit logs — we can share SOC2 docs and our security questionnaire. I'll attach the folder after the call.
[02:36] Samira: For a quick POC, what's the fastest path to test with our data? We have CSVs and a small doc store.
[02:42] Marisa: Free credits, self-serve API keys, sample quickstart repo. You can get tokens and call embeddings/generation in minutes. We also have a managed ingestion guide if you want to test with PII — we recommend masking and using private endpoints for sensitive PII.
[02:57] Priya: If we use hosted with free credits, are those calls logged or retained by Redwood? Data retention policy matters.
[03:03] Derrick: By default hosted stores transient logs for troubleshooting; we have redaction options and can enable no-logging for enterprise pilot, but default retention is 30 days. For private deployments logs stay in your environment.
[03:18] Owen: About cost — we're trying to forecast peak cost. How do batching and quantization affect unit economics?
[03:24] Derrick: Batching reduces per-token CPU/GPU amortization but increases latency; we have smart batching that respects latency SLOs and continuous batching for similar sequences. Quantization reduces memory and can cut cost by 30-60% depending on model. Redwood Optimize can recommend configurations for your workload mix.
[03:45] Priya: Do you have examples of customers who started PLG then moved to Dedicated?
[03:50] Marisa: Yep, several. Typical pattern: PLG hosted for dev+canary, then reserved Dedicated for steady production traffic. We can share case study links.
[03:58] Samira: We want p99 < 300ms for 2-3 token prompts (short highlight extraction) at 50 QPS — is that realistic on hosted?
[04:07] Derrick: At 50 QPS for short prompts you'll likely meet p99 < 300ms on a tuned hosted variant if you use the low-latency model, but it's borderline at sustained peaks. For true predictability we'd recommend Dedicated pool sized for 50 QPS or autoscaling with burst capacity. We should run your sample payloads against hosted to confirm — that's in the action items.
[04:25] Owen: How does the free credits quota look? Can we reserve credits for our team or is it account-level?
[04:30] Marisa: Free credits are account-level; we can issue a pilot credit grant and extend it if needed. For larger pilots we do short-term pilot agreements with committed usage and discounts.
[04:43] Priya: On the security side, we need to include InfoSec in the next call. Who from Redwood should they talk to?
[04:49] Marisa: I'll loop in our security lead and solutions architect. Derrick will be the SE main point for the benchmark.
[04:56] Speaker 1: [overlap] sorry, can you repeat pilot agreement details?
[05:00] Marisa: Sure — short pilots are typically 4-8 weeks, we can do hosted pilot with credits and optional dedicated trial if you need reserved perf. Pilot contract includes data handling, SLA targets, and trial pricing.
[05:14] Priya: For dedicated, do we have to sign a long term commit?
[05:18] Marisa: There's flexibility: monthly reserved capacity or annual with deeper discounts. We can scope minimal reserved to cover baseline and autoscale for bursts.
[05:27] Samira: Any gotchas for embeddings consistency across model updates? We rely on stable vectors.
[05:31] Derrick: Good point — we version models and recommend pinning model ids. If we do model rollouts we provide eval hooks and regression alerts so you can test your vector drift. Redwood Optimize recommends stable quantization when you need consistent vectors.
[05:50] Owen: About private deployment — network setup, VPC peering, and egress — we need to understand latency implications if air-gapped.
[05:57] Derrick: Private (VPC) keeps data inside your cloud and we run the control plane optionally managed. On-prem will be more variable; network hops and local GPU type matter. We can provide an on-prem sizing guide.
[06:08] Priya: Are there any significant differences in API surface between hosted and private?
[06:12] Marisa: No, same API surface. The difference is operational: keys, network, and telemetry location. That parity is intentional so devs don't rewrite code between envs.
[06:23] Priya: Great. Can you describe the quickstart steps we should expect?
[06:27] Marisa: Sign up, claim free credits, run quickstart repo: install SDK, get api_key, run sample embedding/gen calls, check console for token-level costs. Then swap in your prompts and data. We'll give recommended model and quant profiles.
[06:40] Samira: SDK languages? Node, Python?
[06:42] Marisa: Node, Python, Go SDKs and a CLI. Quickstart repo link will be included.
[06:47] Owen: For the latency benchmark — what metrics will Derrick collect?
[06:50] Derrick: p50/p95/p99, cold vs warm start, tokens/sec, error rates, and payload size sensitivity. We'll also note effective cost per call.
[06:58] Priya: Could you run the benchmark with our anonymized sample prompts? We'll upload a small set.
[07:03] Derrick: Yep send them to the shared sheet. I'll run both hosted and a tuned low-latency hosted variant. We can discuss Dedicated sizing if hosted fails to meet p99 consistently.
[07:14] Marisa: Quick note — if you need absolute data residency we recommend starting Private early; otherwise PLG hosted helps you validate UX faster.
[07:23] Priya: Understood. For compliance, if we go hosted for dev we need to ensure anonymization is effective. Is there an ingestion helper?
[07:29] Derrick: We have client libs with redaction helpers and a managed ingestion guide. We'll share examples.
[07:35] Samira: Any rate limiting in trial? We expect bursts during ingestion.
[07:39] Marisa: Standard rate limits apply, but for pilots we can increase limits and set quotas per token. We'll set sensible defaults.
[07:47] Owen: What's the expected turnaround for the pilot contract?
[07:50] Marisa: Usually 3-5 business days for a standard pilot SOW and contract once terms are agreed.
[07:57] Priya: Ok let's talk personnel — who signs off internally for us? I'll loop in InfoSec and procurement. Owen will own platform sizing.
[08:04] Owen: Yep I'll own platform work. Samira will validate models and prompts.
[08:09] Marisa: Great. Any competitive concerns?
[08:12] Priya: Anthropic's models are attractive for safety but OpenAI has stronger tooling — curious how Redwood's hosting compares.
[08:20] Derrick: We provide model catalog with tuned open models plus Redwood-verified performance sheets; you get flexibility to switch between model variants for cost/perf.
[08:30] Speaker 2: This is great. Quick question on observability — do we get token-level cost per route?
[08:35] Marisa: Yes Console provides token-level breakdown, per-route latency, and A/B rollout traces. You can export logs to your SIEM.
[08:42] Priya: Perfect. Could you also include an example SLA for Dedicated?
[08:45] Marisa: We'll attach the SLA doc.
[08:48] Samira: For sampling, what about cold start on higher context windows?
[08:52] Derrick: Cold starts scale with attention complexity; longer contexts increase latency. Our kernel selection and KV cache management mitigate that but it's expected. We'll test your longer sequences as part of the bench.
[09:05] Marisa: Should we summarize next steps?
[09:07] Priya: Yes please.
[09:09] Marisa: Action: Marisa will send pricing and pilot contract, Derrick runs hosted latency benchmark with your anonymized prompts, FastLane provides sample payloads and security contacts. We'll reconvene after bench.
[09:20] Owen: Timeline OK — bench by 05/08, contract by 05/06.
[09:25] Marisa: I'll also share SOC2 and onboarding checklist.
[09:29] Priya: Thanks everyone.
[09:31] Marisa: Thanks, talk soon.
[09:33] [call ends] 

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker overlaps and minor mis-transcriptions (e.g., "k-v cash" instead of "KV cache"). References: shared deck and bench sheet as listed in header.
closing_recital: Recap: start with hosted PLG quickstart using free credits to validate UX + models. Run Redwood SE benchmark with FastLane samples. If latency or custody rules require, move to Dedicated or Private. Security docs and pricing to be shared. Next meeting contingent on benchmark results and security review.
